notes: Zenodo DOI verification pending for v1.4.0.

Fixed: An unclassified direct commit of the first release (no PR that could carry a category, e.g. the init or adoption commit) is listed under Changed with a warning instead of blocking under a publishing policy (KIT-GF-119); from the second release on an unclassified commit still blocks. agentic-kit init starts the new repository on main whatever init.defaultBranch says, so its first commit and the init --github push no longer land on master (KIT-GF-120).

Fixed: The first release of a project without a previous v* tag no longer blocks release run in A2 (KIT-GF-118, owner decision 2026-11-15): without a previous tag the release is the first release, its notes start at the root commit (release-notes-generate --first-release, also transfer standard-error-scan --first-release) and list commits without a PR number as direct commits instead of blocking, only in the first release. Release tags the origin lists but the clone lacks block. The B4 gate carries first_release (range, root commit, direct commits), which the approval signature binds; init still creates no tag. Journey J6 (G4) runs init, the signed recovery with --publication none, the CI update and release run up to the B4 gate of the first release, without a hand tag or hand configuration; journey run steps may name a working directory inside the run root (cwd).

Added: workspace init --publication <policy> writes the publication policy (none, github, github+pypi, github+pypi+zenodo; default unchanged) into the new manifest, also for the signed recovery of a generated project (--recover-partial), whose signature binds the policy. Routes that name the recovery keep the option, an invalid value fails before any write (INVALID_PUBLICATION), a recovery of an initialized workspace does not change its policy, and workspace remove recognizes the generated manifest with any policy. Nobody has to edit .agentic/config.yaml by hand to choose a policy (owner decision 2026-11-15 for journey J6).

Workflow friction (owner plan 2026-11-13, slice 1): check-producer directory with CI law (G1); work finish without --path publishes existing commits (K1), always sets a release-note category from the branch kind (K2) and reports Unreleased lines the release gate would reject at the PR (G2); curated release sections no longer need three keyword categories (K3, owner E2 b); kit update writes the adoption line into Unreleased in curated workspaces (K4); transfer commit retries a held index.lock five times (K5); BLOCKED results name the resolving command (G3).

Workflow friction slice 2a: work finish rebuilds the docs-pages projection after the handoff commit and commits any change before the PR, so the site staleness check has a producer on the standard path (G1, KIT-CHK-SITE-PROJECTION-FRESH).

Workflow friction slice 2c: journey contracts (G4) run fixed workflows against the built wheel in a disposable workspace with a local origin — J1 (start, change, finish) and J3 (change already committed, then finish) — and fail CI on a BLOCKED step or a changed approval count; J2, J4 and J5 are listed as pending.

Workflow friction slice 2c, journey J2 (G4): J2 adopts a Kit release in a curated workspace with real wheels from a loopback index (kit update plan and signed execution), plans the finish, emulates the merge with git and handoff steps and requires release ready to pass with only the adoption line; approvals now count signed executions and effects beyond none/fetch/push/network_read (owner decision 2026-11-13), so J2 needs two consents offline.

Fixed: The managed workspace CI keys its pip cache on its managed source .agentic/ci/agentic-gate.yaml, so actions/setup-python no longer fails in a generic workspace without requirements.txt or pyproject.toml (G4 live-run preflight); kit update and workspace ci-update refresh the previous Kit-written template.

Workflow friction slice 2b (G3): a BLOCKED or FAIL result without a resolving Kit command carries the human marker (next_command_kind human, empty next_command, mandatory next_command_reason); routed results say next_command_kind kit. The work orchestrators, release ready, release prepare and transfer commit comply; a ratchet test lists the remaining orchestrators as debt that may only shrink.

Workflow friction slice 2b, second step (G3): _emit of the work/release commands and of kit update, kit return-install and kit return-revert routes every BLOCKED or FAIL payload before printing (blocked_route.with_route), so release run, release abandon, work rescue and the three kit commands comply; the ratchet checks the emitter by AST and its debt list drops from 32 to 26. The human-marker reason of a step that printed a Kit summary now names its STATE= and NEXT= instead of the banner line.

Fixed: work start no longer blocks when origin was added after workspace init and nothing else changed (F1): check_projection classifies the difference as projection_identity_bound_after_init, and work finish regenerates the successor package with the origin identity in the same work cycle. Any other changed input still blocks.

Fixed: The CI of projects generated with agentic-kit init --github-actions keys its pip cache on .github/workflows/ci.yml and pyproject.toml, so actions/setup-python no longer fails for the generic and governance-wrapper types without a dependency file (F2).

Workflow friction, transfer orchestrators (G3): transfer pr-complete, pr-create-complete, pr-closeout-complete, post-merge-complete, post-merge-settle, evidence-pr-complete, sync-main, remote-work-start, remote-next, admin-refresh-pr and chat-switch-complete print only through the routing emitter _emit_transfer, so every BLOCKED or FAIL result names its resolving Kit command or carries the human marker with a reason, in JSON and as text lines; a missing rule confirmation names agentic-kit rules acknowledge. The ratchet accepts delegates that print only through routing emitters; its debt list shrinks from 26 to 15.

Workflow friction K6: a CI wait that times out before any check left the queue reports ci_state NOT_STARTED instead of a plain timeout. transfer pr-complete and pr-create-complete then name agentic-kit pr wait-ci <PR> as a retry within the consent already given, with a reason that sends a person to GitHub Actions if the queue stays stuck; slow CI (PENDING) names the same command, NOT_RUN names pr rerun-checks (signed approval), failed CI keeps the human marker. work finish and release run keep the Kit route of a blocked nested result, and the human-marker reason of work reads the STATE:/NEXT: transfer summary block.

Workflow friction G2: release checks that depend only on repository content run at the PR. work finish runs transfer standard-error-scan without --before-release and the Kit CI pin guard of release prepare before the commit (KIT-CHK-RELEASE-CONTENT-AT-PR); on the branches of a release run whose A2 passed the step is a no-op. reference/check-producers.json lists every step of release ready, release prepare and the --before-release scan under release_path with its stage; a test derives the steps from the source, so a new release check must be run at the PR or listed with its reason.

Workflow friction K7 + J4: release run resumes a B4 that stopped before its release PR. After a stop behind the release commit (nothing pushed, or pushed without a PR) the B4 gate offers a signed resume (resume-unpublished-release-commits) that commits projection files B4 left uncommitted with B4's own subject and publishes the existing commits with work finish (K1), instead of blocking with changed-paths-drift. Both B4 resumes (K7 and the open-PR resume of release 1.1.4) accept a linear history on the approved base: the release commit with exactly the approved paths (approved directories included), then only handoff or docs-pages projection commits; whether the branch exists on the origin is read with git ls-remote, so the GitHub lookup runs only when a PR can exist. Journey J4 (G4) runs a release run in the release fixture, interrupts B4 by a refused push and requires the resume gate; the retest runner confines that fixture's remotes to the run's temporary root and drops GH_REPO/GH_HOST.

Workflow friction K8 + J5: the Kit's own release takes the workspace route. Its curated summary is the Unreleased section, so release run needs no summary lines. work finish stops a PR with a product category (Added, Changed, Fixed, Breaking) in a curated workspace that adds no Unreleased line (KIT-CHK-CURATED-UNRELEASED-LINE). The changelog hygiene test reads shipped findings from the catalog instead of any mention in a released section. Journey J5 releases a curated workspace with exactly one line; no journey is pending.

Workflow friction, workspace orchestrators (G3): workspace adopt, dpa-intake, init, remove and upgrade, docs lifecycle sweep and dpa final-closeout-check print only through the routing emitter emit_routed. Every result that ends one of them with a non-zero exit names its way on, also under its own status name (BLOCK, BLOCKED_FOR_DPA_INTAKE): a planning run of workspace upgrade, workspace init or workspace remove where one resolves it, otherwise the human marker with a reason. The ratchet's debt list shrinks from 15 to 8.

Workflow friction, single commands (G3): artifact-gc, chat session-start, workflow go, release-prep, release-publish and post-release-doi-closeout print only through emit_routed. Every result that ends one of them with a non-zero exit names its way on: a busy state or failed step of workflow go names workflow status --explain, a DOI closeout before the release and its DOIs are verified names post-release-check, everything else carries the human marker with the refused path, blocker or error. release-prep and release-publish JSON now also carry result_status; workflow go refuses with exit 2 as before, now with a route. The ratchet's debt list shrinks from 8 to 2 (init, github-create).

Workflow friction, project creation (G3): init and github-create are orchestrators with --json and result_status, and print only through emit_routed. JSON mode never asks: a missing project name blocks, the description defaults to <name> project, and a public repository needs the new --confirm-public. Invalid options, a missing Git, a non-empty target directory, a missing or signed-out gh and a refused public repository block with the human marker before anything is written (exit 2 for invalid input, 1 for a refusal or gh); a failing gh repo create after the project exists fails with the github-create retry in its reason. Text mode keeps the questions, asks for a public repository before creating the project, and reports refusals as Error: … plus route lines on stderr; gh and git init output is captured. The ratchet's debt list is empty.

Workflow friction K9: every entry of the finding catalog carries a validated one-line title. greenfield status without --json prints one line per finding (id, Kit state, fixed in, title) instead of a Python dict; the JSON output and the status packaged in the wheel carry the title, so a workspace can read the catalog without the Kit's reports.

Fixed: transfer post-merge-complete reports BLOCKED with a human route instead of PASS when the final known-volatile cleanup fails after a passing lifecycle (exit 2 as before, KIT-GF-112), and artifact-gc answers an unreadable --older-than with a routed FAIL_INVALID_OLDER_THAN result instead of a Click usage error (KIT-GF-113). The finding catalog records the fixes of #2782 and of F1 and F2 (#2786) as KIT-GF-109 to KIT-GF-111, each with an installed-wheel machine contract.

Fixed: G3 remedy table (g3_remedies): a BLOCKED or FAIL whose cause a Kit command resolves names it as next_command. workspace init over an init project names the signed recovery (KIT-GF-114), a recovery with --inject-ci names the recovery without the flag and workspace ci-update --inject-ci --execute (KIT-GF-115), and a release run B4 stop names the plan run that offers the resume (KIT-GF-116). The manifest lists push and release_publish for init and github-create; init without --github stays without remote effects, so journeys count init --github as a consent (KIT-GF-117).

findings.gap: command_argv executes any argv. safety: READ_ONLY is a label and is not enforced. remote-next/rn and typed-next run the queued order without an --execute step.
findings.probe: touch EXECUTED ran under safety: READ_ONLY

findings.gap: cockpit_action passes the order's own allow_bounded to run_cockpit_action, so an order authorises its own BOUNDED actions, for example dialog.rnc (commit and push closeout paths) or dialog.rn (run the next order).
log_path is checked with startswith("docs/reports/terminal/") only; docs/reports/terminal/../../../../x writes outside the repository.
findings.probe: log file created outside the repository root for both runners

findings.gap: The required gates are substring checks on the command; echo pytest ruff check check-docs doctor; … satisfies the contract without running a gate. This defeats the gate contract, not a security boundary, because the lane executes shell by design.

Raw git/gh and interpreters are recognised only by literal argv[0] or text prefix. env git push --force, /usr/bin/git push, git -c … push, git -C . push, env gh pr merge, /usr/bin/python3 -c, .venv/bin/python -c pass parsing and lint; git -c/git -C produce only a WARN. This contradicts transfer_safety_rules.yaml ("Do not put raw gh … into LLM-to-local payloads").
findings.probe: all seven argv vectors reach execution

findings.gap: Paths are checked lexically; symlinks are followed. A payload symlink copies any readable file into the repository, where a later commit can publish it, and a symlinked directory makes the write land outside the repository.
findings.probe: secret copied into docs/leak.txt; file planted outside the root

findings.gap: _head_matches accepts any prefix of HEAD, including one character (short_head.startswith(value)), so an anchor matches about one HEAD in sixteen without any knowledge of the current state.
findings.probe: _head_matches("a", …) is true for a HEAD starting with a

findings.gap: (a) The freshness guard (status, kind, expected branch, anchor) runs only when no branch is given; transfer continue always passes the inferred branch, so on the canonical path the guard is skipped. (b) Without a branch, the guard validates the order in the current checkout, and the order executed is re-read after git switch and git pull of the order's branch, with no re-validation.
findings.probe: an order without status, kind or anchor executed with branch=; a different order executed than the one validated

findings.gap: The validator is a text denylist over an arbitrary Python script ('git push', 'os.system(', …). subprocess.run(["git", "push", …]) or __import__("o"+"s") pass. The lane is unrestricted by nature; the validator must not be presented as a safety boundary.

mitigations.summary: Typed command_argv and transfer run_command run READ_ONLY Kit commands and read-only git/gh queries. BOUNDED Kit commands, BOUNDED cockpit actions and commands outside the manifest need the local --allow-unlisted flag on transfer continue, transfer remote-next, transfer apply, transfer run-local, remote-next/rn, work-order typed-next and work-order typed-run. DESTRUCTIVE Kit commands, raw git/gh mutations and interpreters are refused even with the flag. The refusal happens before any action of the order runs.

The anchor must be a full 40-character hash. It must equal HEAD for an uncommitted order, and otherwise the first parent of the commit that last changed the order file. transfer remote-next checks status, kind, branch and anchor again after switch and pull, on every path including an explicit or inferred branch (transfer continue). The order that runs is therefore the order that was checked. transfer order-validate uses the same binding.

work-order run --execute, the next-turn.py fixed slot (next_turn_runner, GUI work-order run) and current.sh (agent_command_runner) no longer execute anything. They report BLOCKED_RETIRED_LANE, keep their evidence and point to typed work orders, transfer orders and the planner executor. The validators stay as format checks. The commands are removed after the deprecation window.
